pictures.scene: Anthonissen, The Beached Whale — a huge stranded whale lying on the sand with a crowd of townspeople gathered round it and a man standing up on its back while boats ride offshore under a pale sky, then i saw a beast with ten horns and seven heads, rising out of the sea
pictures.name: pd_anthonissen_leviathan

pictures.scene: Rembrandt circle, The Man with the Golden Helmet — an old soldier standing against deep black in an ornate gleaming gold helmet with red-brown plumes, his face half lost in shadow beneath the brim, there were ten royal crowns on its horns, and blasphemous names on its heads
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_circle_the_man_with_the_golden_helmet

pictures.scene: Delacroix, Lion Devouring a Goat — a tawny lion crouched low over the dark goat it has pulled down on the open ground, under a grey storm sky with blue hills behind, the beast i saw was like a leopard, with the feet of a bear and the mouth of a lion
pictures.name: pd_delacroix_lion_devouring_a_goat

pictures.scene: A judgment seat — a pale stone seat raised on a stepped platform with four torches burning around it on a dark hillside under an empty pale sky, and the dragon gave the beast his power, and his throne and great authority
pictures.name: judgment_seat

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Raising of Lazarus — Christ standing with his hand lifted high as Lazarus rises pale out of the open grave and the onlookers start back with their arms thrown up in the half-dark, one of the heads of the beast appeared to be mortally wounded, but the mortal wound was healed
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_raising_of_lazarus

pictures.scene: Poussin, The Adoration of the Golden Calf — a pale calf set up on a garlanded altar with a ring of dancers swinging round it in bright robes while a priest in white points up at it, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast, they worshiped the dragon who had given authority to the beast
pictures.name: pd_poussin_golden_calf

pictures.scene: Francken, The Worship of the Idol — a golden seated idol high on a carved pedestal with a crowned king in red and ermine bowing before it among his courtiers while incense smoke drifts across the hall, and they worshiped the beast, saying, who is like the beast
pictures.name: pd_francken_idol

pictures.scene: Uccello, The Battle of San Romano — a white horse rearing among armoured lancers with broken lances crossing the air and fallen armour lying on the ground while hares bolt through the hedges behind, and who can wage war against it, the beast was given a mouth to speak arrogant and blasphemous words
pictures.name: pd_uccello_the_battle_of_san_romano

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Belshazzar's Feast — a turbaned and crowned king in a jewelled gold mantle twisting round from the table with his hands flung out and his eyes wide at the writing on the wall, and authority to act for 42 months, and the beast opened its mouth to speak blasphemies against God
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Durer, The Adoration of the Trinity — the Father holding up the crucified Christ in a ring of angels while saints and martyrs and popes and kings adore from the clouds on either side, and to slander his name and his tabernacle, those who dwell in heaven
pictures.name: pd_durer_all_saints

pictures.scene: Gerome, The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer — a lone lion padding out onto the sand of a packed arena with torches burning along the wall at the left and a grey sky over the crowded tiers, then the beast was permitted to wage war against the saints, and to conquer them
pictures.name: pd_gerome_martyrs

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Tower of Babel — a vast spiralling brick tower half built and half crumbling rising over a harbour town with cranes and scaffolds and tiny workmen on every tier, and it was given authority over every tribe and people, and tongue and nation
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Repin, Religious Procession in Kursk Province — a dusty crowd pressing forward behind tall gold banners and a carried icon with a priest in gold vestments in the middle and a lame boy on a crutch pushing in at the edge, and all who dwell on the earth will worship the beast, all whose names have not been written from the foundation of the world
pictures.name: pd_repin_religious_procession_in_kursk_province

pictures.scene: Van Eyck, The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb — the Ghent altarpiece with Mary reading and God enthroned in red and John the Baptist above, and below them the Lamb standing on the altar among censing angels while crowds come in from every side, in the book of life belonging to the lamb who was slain, he who has an ear
pictures.name: pd_van_eyck_the_adoration_of_the_mystic_lamb

pictures.scene: Munkacsy, Christ before Pilate — Christ standing bound and silent in white while the accusing crowd presses in shouting and pointing at him and the governor watches from his seat, let him hear, if anyone is destined for captivity
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_christ_before_pilate

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Saint Paul in Prison — the old apostle sitting in a bare cell with heavy books at his feet and a manuscript on his knee and a quill in his hand, light falling on the rough wall behind him, into captivity he will go, if anyone is to die by the sword
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_saint_paul_in_prison

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — Judas gripping Christ to kiss him as soldiers in polished black armour reach in out of the night and a man flees crying out at the left, by the sword he must be killed, here is a call for the perseverance and faith of the saints
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Zurbaran, Agnus Dei — a young ram with curled horns lying bound by its feet on a grey stone slab against a plain black ground, its head turned quietly aside, then i saw another beast rising out of the earth, this beast had two horns like a lamb
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_agnus_dei

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint George and the Dragon — a knight on a rearing white horse driving his lance down into a black winged dragon writhing on the ground beneath the hooves, but spoke like a dragon, and this beast exercised all the authority of the first beast
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_george_and_the_dragon

pictures.scene: Bellini, Procession in Piazza San Marco — a long double line of grey-robed brothers with candles carrying a gold reliquary under its canopy across the wide square in front of the domes of San Marco, and caused the earth and those who dwell in it, to worship the first beast
pictures.name: pd_bellini_procession_piazza_san_marco

pictures.scene: Tintoretto, Moses Striking the Rock — the old prophet in red with his arms flung wide and his rod at the rock while water breaks out over the crowd in white gathered below with their jars, whose mortal wound had been healed, and the second beast performed great signs
pictures.name: pd_tintoretto_moses_striking_the_rock

pictures.scene: Martin, The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah — a curtain of fire pouring out of a black sky over a ruined city far below while one small white figure flees across the bare rocks in the foreground, to cause even fire from heaven to come down to earth, in the presence of the people
pictures.name: pd_martin_the_destruction_of_sodom_and_gomorrah

pictures.scene: Steen, Beware of Luxury — a woman in black leaning over a seated man reading while a pig noses among the cards and pretzels scattered on the floor and a monkey meddles with the clock above the door, because of the signs it was given to perform on behalf of the first beast, it deceived those who dwell on the earth
pictures.name: pd_steen_beware_of_luxury

pictures.scene: Robert, The Statue — a draped classical figure standing high on its pedestal among dark cypresses and broken ruins while washerwomen work at the basin far below it, telling them to make an image to the beast, that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived
pictures.name: pd_robert_statue

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Daniel and Cyrus before the Idol of Bel — a turbaned crowned king in a heavy gold cloak pointing his sceptre up at the idol on its altar while Daniel bows low at his side in the shadow, the second beast was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so that the image could speak
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_idol_bel

pictures.scene: Surikov, The Morning of the Streltsy Execution — condemned men in white shirts holding lit candles in the carts before the domes of Saint Basil's while women weep in the mud around them and a child in a red headscarf stares, and cause all who refused to worship it to be killed, and the second beast required all people small and great
pictures.name: pd_surikov_the_morning_of_the_streltsy_execution

pictures.scene: Maes, The Spinner — an old woman working at her spinning wheel beside a red-clothed table in a plain room with pots standing on the shelf behind her, rich and poor, free and slave, to receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead
pictures.name: pd_maes_handen

pictures.scene: Van Reymerswaele, A Moneychanger and His Wife — a moneychanger in a red fur-trimmed cap weighing coins on a small hand balance while his wife in a white coif leans in over the heaps of gold and silver spread on the green cloth, so that no one could buy or sell unless he had the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name
pictures.name: pd_van_reymerswaele_a_moneychanger_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Philosopher in Meditation — an old bearded scholar sitting still and thinking beside a tall sunlit window in a vaulted room with a winding stair climbing into the shadow behind him, here is a call for wisdom, let the one who has insight calculate the number of the beast
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_filosoof

pictures.scene: Vermeer, Woman Holding a Balance — a woman in blue with a white hood standing at a table of pearls and gold holding an empty balance steady in her hand, with a dark painting of the last judgment hanging on the wall behind her, for it is the number of a man, and that number is 666
pictures.name: pd_vermeer_balance

lines.text: Then I saw a beast with ten horns and seven heads
rising out of the sea.
There were ten royal crowns on its horns
and blasphemous names on its heads.
The beast I saw was like a leopard,
with the feet of a bear and the mouth of a lion.
And the dragon gave the beast his power
and his throne and great authority.
One of the heads of the beast appeared to be mortally wounded.
But the mortal wound was healed,
and the whole world marveled and followed the beast.
They worshiped the dragon who had given authority to the beast,
and they worshiped the beast, saying,
Who is like the beast,
and who can wage war against it?
The beast was given a mouth to speak arrogant and blasphemous words,
and authority to act for 42 months.
And the beast opened its mouth to speak blasphemies against God
and to slander His name and His tabernacle,
those who dwell in heaven.
Then the beast was permitted to wage war against the saints
and to conquer them,
and it was given authority over every tribe and people
and tongue and nation.
And all who dwell on the earth will worship the beast,
all whose names have not been written from the foundation of the world
in the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain.
He who has an ear,
let him hear:
If anyone is destined for captivity,
into captivity he will go;
if anyone is to die by the sword,
by the sword he must be killed.
Here is a call for the perseverance and faith of the saints.
Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth.
This beast had two horns like a lamb,
but spoke like a dragon.
And this beast exercised all the authority of the first beast
and caused the earth and those who dwell in it
to worship the first beast,
whose mortal wound had been healed.
And the second beast performed great signs
to cause even fire from heaven to come down to earth
in the presence of the people.
Because of the signs it was given to perform on behalf of the first beast,
it deceived those who dwell on the earth,
telling them to make an image to the beast
that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived.
The second beast was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast,
so that the image could speak
and cause all who refused to worship it to be killed.
And the second beast required all people small and great,
rich and poor, free and slave,
to receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,
so that no one could buy or sell unless he had the mark,
the name of the beast or the number of its name.
Here is a call for wisdom:
Let the one who has insight calculate the number of the beast,
for it is the number of a man,
and that number is 666.
